video_goal: A visual guide demonstrating how to bleed the front hydraulic brake lines on a 2022 Yamaha YZF-R3.
required_subjects_and_props: 2022 Yamaha YZF-R3 motorcycle, Phillips screwdriver, DOT 4 brake fluid, 8mm box wrench, clear plastic tubing, fluid catch bottle, protective gloves

outline_steps.visual_action: Focus on the right handlebar of a 2022 Yamaha YZF-R3, highlighting the rectangular front brake fluid reservoir.
Gloved hands use a Phillips screwdriver to unscrew the two top screws, lifting the metal cap and rubber diaphragm off the reservoir.
Hands pour fresh DOT 4 brake fluid from a plastic bottle into the open reservoir until the liquid reaches the upper 'MAX' line.
Pan down to the front wheel's brake caliper. A hand slides an 8mm box wrench over the hexagonal base of the metal bleeder valve.
Fingers push a piece of clear plastic tubing tightly over the nipple of the bleeder valve, with the tube trailing down into a plastic catch bottle.
Looking down at the right handlebar, a hand squeezes the front brake lever in and out three times, then holds it squeezed tightly against the throttle grip.
Down at the caliper, while the lever is held off-screen, a hand pushes the 8mm wrench a quarter-turn counterclockwise to open the valve.
Dark brake fluid mixed with small air bubbles shoots out of the bleeder valve nipple and travels down the clear plastic tubing.
The hand immediately pulls the 8mm wrench a quarter-turn clockwise, tightening the bleeder valve shut.
Back at the handlebar, the hand slowly releases the squeezed front brake lever, allowing it to extend fully outward.
Looking into the open reservoir, the fluid level visibly drops. The hand pours more DOT 4 fluid from the bottle to restore the level to the 'MAX' line.
Hands place the rubber diaphragm and metal cap back onto the reservoir, then use the Phillips screwdriver to tighten the two screws securely.
